OVERVIEW

[
1
]

Who is Uncle Ludwig? Where was he during World
War II? What was he doing during the War? Why was Defendant Glenn Joseph (or
Joseph
[1]
)
Feldman
(Mr. Feldman)
so interested in the answers to these questions?
The first three questions became an obsession for Mr. Feldman. The fourth is
the one that the Court needs to consider more fully.

[
2
]

Unfortunately, the proof administered
demonstrates that Mr. Feldman was asking too many questions and drawing
conclusions from too few answers.

[
3
]

Friends since the age of 15, after meeting at
Paré Lanes, and longtime business partners, the friendship of the Co-plaintiff,
Irwin Lande
(Mr. Lande)
and Mr. Feldman came to a crashing end in the
fall of 2019.

[
4
]

How this came to pass will be related in the
present judgment. Safe to say that the disagreement between the two partners
was more than a temporary tiff.

[
5
]

Mr. Feldman believes that the lifestyle of Mr.
Lande and his wife, the Co-plaintiff Claude-Andrée Pion
(Ms. Pion)
can
only be possible because they are living off the avails of gold illegally
stolen by the Nazis from Jewish people, Holocaust victims of the Nazi regime,
during World War II. This gold would have been brought to Canada by Dr. Ludwig
Delphiner, a cousin of Mr. Lande, in the form of gold bars that he stored in a
bunker in his home on Ile Bizard
(the Nazi Gold)
.

[
6
]

Dr. Delphiner immigrated to Canada in 1926. This
notwithstanding, Mr. Feldman alleges that Dr. Delphiner was a Nazi SS
officer who participated in the thefts, believing that he returned to Europe to
serve with the Nazis during the War.

[
7
]

The gold bars, or the proceeds thereof, would
have been inherited by Martin Lande
(Martin)
, the father of Mr. Lande
and ultimately by his wife, Mia Lande
(Mia)
. Their children, Mr. Lande
and his sister, Sherry Feifer
(Sherry),
would ultimately have inherited
these supposedly vast amounts of gold from their mother.

[
8
]

Mr. Lande and Ms. Pion seek compensatory damages
in the amount of $13 million and exemplary damages in the amount of $3 million.
They also seek the reimbursement of certain of their legal fees.

1.

the context

1.1

The Background of the Lande Family

[
9
]

Martin and Mia lost many family members in the
Holocaust, including their fathers. They survived the concentration and death
camps and following a short sojourn in Israel after the war, they immigrated to
Canada in the early fifties; they were among the few survivors in the family.

[
10
]

Following their arrival in Canada, Martin and
Mia worked very hard to establish their business and to provide for their
family. They were not wealthy, at least at the beginning of their life here.
Martin eventually established a business, called Famous Leather Products,
building it up to a point where it employed 60 to 70 people. He passed in 1996,
but Sherry and Mia continued the business for a time, essentially to wind it
down.

[
11
]

When Mia passed in 2015, with the
inter vivos

gifts that he had received and his inheritance, Mr. Lande estimates that he
received around $15 million from his mother.

[
12
]

Growing-up, Mr. Lande’s home was one where the
Jewish faith was both important and practiced. The horror of the Holocaust was
part of Mr. Lande’s and Sherry’s education. His parents were proud of their
Jewish faith and heritage. They believed that it was important for the entire
family to understand and embrace the Jewish faith and passed their values down
to their children.

[
13
]

Mr. Lande has continued to practice the Jewish
religion and to follow Jewish traditions in his own family life. He and Ms.
Pion are not regular attendees at Synagogue but attend for the High Holidays.
Mr. Lande has a seat in the Synagogue and when he is present may be asked to
participate in the service.

[
14
]

He and Ms. Pion have four children who have all
been brought up in the Jewish faith. The boys each had a Bar Mitzvah and the
girls a Bat Mitzvah.

[
15
]

For Ms. Pion, Judaism is not about attending the
Synagogue, but rather it is a way of life. Before the allegations, she would
often invite people to the home for Shabbat. Since Mr. Feldman began to
disseminate his allegations, the tradition of attending these regular Friday
evening gatherings is mostly limited to family.

1.2

Ms. Pion’s Conversion to Judaism

[
16
]

Before marrying Mr. Lande, some eight years
after they met, Ms. Pion, brought up as a Catholic, wanted to convert to
Judaism. It was important to her that she be accepted by the Lande family,
particularly Mia.

[
17
]

The conversion process took well over three
years, with classes each week, but Ms. Pion was rewarded with a close
relationship with Mia and Sherry. She had to work hard to be accepted in the Jewish
community, but through her commitment was successful. Mia assisted greatly with
this process.

1.3

The Lande’s Life After the Allegations

[
18
]

Before Mr. Feldman began to disseminate his
story, the Landes had a busy social calendar, with at least weekly invitations,
mostly in the Jewish community. These have largely disappeared since the
allegations, to the point that the invitations that they now receive are
largely from outside this community.

[
19
]

Because of their infrequent attendance, the
Landes cannot really say how the story has affected the perception of them at
the Synagogue. It has affected the perception of them in the larger Montreal
Jewish community.

[
20
]

At the Bar Mitzvah for one of the sons in the
fall of 2019, people were talking about the Nazi Gold allegations, even while
attending the celebration in the Lande’s home. Fortunately, Mr. Feldman advised
Ms. Pion that he would not attend, saving her the embarrassment of having to
withdraw his invitation. Nonetheless, the talk of the Nazi Gold in their home
was disquieting.

[
21
]

Ms. Pion identified numerous Jewish families
from whom they no longer receive invitations. It would not be appropriate or
useful to list them in the present judgment, but she recalled at least 10
Jewish families who questioned them on the story and no longer call them. One
of the concerns that Ms. Pion raises, as to the motivation of their friends for
disassociating with them, is their fear about being on the wrong side of Mr. Feldman.
His attempt to disrupt a Jewish wedding is but one example of how far he is
prepared to go when he is displeased.
[2]

[
22
]

Ms. Pion also recounted how her own family
members began to question her about the family’s lifestyle. They wondered if
she knew everything about her husband. She believes that they may have doubts
about the real source of the Landes’ wealth.

[
23
]

While Mr. Lande was able to identify fewer lost
friendships than his wife, he did ultimately recall several. The loss of these
friendships is doubly important, as these people might also be potential investors
in business opportunities. Mr. Lande feels that he can no longer approach them.

[
24
]

Mr. Lande believes that, since the allegations
of Mr. Feldman, the focus that he has had to put on them, and more importantly
their potential implications for his family and its security, have made him
less effective in business. Mr. Lande says that he does not have the energy to
suss out new investment opportunities.

[
25
]

The security of the family is a big concern. Mr.
Lande was and remains frightened for his family and his property.

[
26
]

The Lande’s home has been publicly identified
and associated with the storage of gold bars, including in an article in Le
Journal de Montréal. There have been people taking pictures of the home and
stalking it. There was even an incident where graffiti was plastered all over
it; not “artful” graffiti but pure slurs. The “artists” were wearing masks and
could not be identified. Curiously, they filmed or took pictures of their work.
[3]

[
27
]

The picture taking is similar to the modus
operandi used by the “No Feldman wedding video”, referred to above, but Mr.
Feldman denies any involvement.

[
28
]

The Landes arranged for security surveillance of
their home for a time after this incident.

[
29
]

There was an attempt to break into the Landes’
home in 2020 and another in 2022.

[
30
]

Mr. Lande attributes the activity at his home,
like the graffiti, to Mr. Feldman. He made a complaint to the police on
December 20, 2019, and ultimately Mr. Feldman was arrested.

[
31
]

A friend of Mr. Feldman’s, Guissepe Boccardi, a
police officer, witnessed the arrest. Mr. Feldman was allowed to return home
with his dog and then go to the police station. Apparently, Mr. Lande was
disappointed that Mr. Feldman was not led away in handcuffs and questioned the
police officer as to why this was not the case.

[
32
]

Following another arrest on July 5, 2021, Mr.
Feldman pleaded guilty to one count of criminally harassing Mr. Lande between
September 8, 2019 and June 24, 2020. He was sentenced on April 20, 2022.

[
33
]

At the time of the diffusion of the allegations
the Lande’s children were 20, 18, 16 and 13 years old and were all living at
home.

[
34
]

To summarize, the dissemination of the Nazi Gold
story has been very difficult for Mr. Lande, Ms. Pion and their family. Mr.
Lande reports being anxious, sleeping poorly, having nightmares and that his
relationship with his wife and children has been affected. His wife relates
similar consequences of the allegations and their aftermath.

[
35
]

There is more stress in the home, including on
the part of the children. They are anxious.

[
36
]

The Landes felt compelled to put their dream
home on the market;
[4]

yet this was the home where they expected to spend the rest of their days.

1.4

Who is Uncle Ludwig Delphiner?

[
37
]

Dr. Delphiner seems to have arrived in Canada in
1926, disembarking from an ocean voyage in Halifax.
[5]
He made his way to Montreal
and joined Abbott Laboratories, where he rose through the ranks of the company.
He became a naturalized citizen in 1932.
[6]

[
38
]

Mr. Lande knew Dr. Delphiner growing up; he
recalls a childhood moment where Dr. Delphiner gave Mia one of his cars after
Sherry had been in an accident with Mia’s brand-new Mustang. Over the years, he
made perhaps ten visits to Dr. Delphiner’s home; Mr. Lande does not recall seeing
any bunker there.

[
39
]

Mr. Lande was also present in the home after Dr.
Delphiner’s death, when Mr. Feldman was preparing an inventory, having been
retained by Martin to probate the will. He believes that his father received an
amount of around $900,000 before taxes.

1.5

The Business Relationship

[
40
]

Mr. Feldman recounted his early days with Mr.
Lande to the Court. After meeting Mr. Lande, he spent a lot of time in the
Lande home, but always felt that Mia did not like him much. Yet, he and Mr.
Lande were like brothers and did everything together.

[
41
]

He worked hard to pay for his education and later
to build up his law practice. At the same time, Mr. Feldman was getting into
the real estate business with Mr. Lande.

[
42
]

They bought their first building together in the
early 1980s. Their company was known as Landfeld and they also had a property
management component, LGIF.

[
43
]

Between then and 2019, they bought many more properties,
not without the odd tiff. They do not agree on the work contribution that each
made to the business, but that is not an issue that is particularly important
for the present judgment. Mr. Lande believes that he did more, as Mr. Feldman
was busy with his law practice. The latter also lived in Los Angeles for a
while. Mr. Feldman believes that Mr. Lande did little valuable work,
particularly when he was renovating his home.

[
44
]

Mr. Feldman also spent considerable time
describing his role in the partners’ real estate business, but this is of
limited relevance to the issues before the Court.

1.5.1

The End of the Relationship

[
45
]

Things really changed when Mr. Feldman began to
believe that Mr. Lande was living off gold stolen from Jewish people during the
Holocaust.

[
46
]

Roy Potts, a property manager and long-term
employee of Landfeld, was aware of the Nazi Gold story and the resolution that
the other partners signed in relation to an important property of the partners
(the
Sainte-Catherine Street building)
, which the Court will discuss shortly. It
followed a significant degradation in the relationship between Mr. Feldman and
Mr. Lande. Being in the office, he was able to observe Mr. Feldman recounting
the Nazi Gold story to many people, including bankers and potential tenants.
For Mr. Potts, the way Mr. Feldman told his story made it seem believable.

[
47
]

The fallout from the story was not good for the
business. There was a lot of tension at the office, and it was hard for Mr.
Potts to get instructions when he needed to, particularly after Mr. Feldman
moved out of the office.

[
48
]

In addition, to operate a successful real estate
portfolio, owners need lenders. Mr. Lande believes that he was very
effective in this aspect of the business. He developed a very good relationship
with Desjardins. However, this soured after Mr. Feldman’s allegations in
2019. It seems that Mr. Lande no longer has access to Desjardins credit
facilities. The relationships that he had with his contacts at Desjardins have
been destroyed.

[
49
]

The soured relationship meant that the partners
could no longer share the same office space. Mr. Lande believes that Mr.
Feldman went so far as to put dog excrement on his door handle, although he did
not see him do it.

1.6

Mr. Feldman’s Conduct in 2019 and Beyond

[
50
]

After becoming aware of the inheritance received
by Mr. Lande from Mia’s estate, or perhaps when Mr. Lande began to spend large
sums of money to renovate his home, Mr. Feldman’s behaviour toward his friend
changed. Mr. Lande explains this by saying that Mr. Feldman believed that the
two of them were 50/50 partners in everything, including the money that he
inherited. Certain documents in the record, including a text message from Mr.
Feldman to Mr. Lande in September 2019, give credence to this notion:

Monday morning I want a Cheque for
50% of whatever you inherited from Uncle Ludwig and whatever dividends or
capital gains derived therefrom by Mia and Martin. Atter all I was more than
50% involved in the effort. Don't u think? In fact perhaps I deserve 95% of the
40 million price tag on the sale of your home for all of the hours I put in
with Carol, Douglas and Mustapha while you were busy renovating our corporate
home head quarters. ?? I can agree on monthly installments over 60 months. Let
me know when the Cheques are ready. I figure $90,000 was just a cheap tip for
the efforts, risks and results carol and I delivered for Ludwig. What do you
think. We can discuss this on the way to the polar bear club. Oh yes. Another
$59,000 for the cigars I bought and shared with you at the office. When can I
start spending the money and buying some of those Elvis jackets you wear ??

[…]

You have only three options the way
I see it. Either; 1/ Get me a accounting of the Ludwig and Mia estate and
settle up 50/50. 2/ make a voluntary disclosure to the police authorities. 3/ l
will. Two weeks for you to decide.
[7]

[
51
]

Mr. Lande felt as though he was being extorted
and showed the text to his wife.  She describes the relationship between Mr.
Lande and Mr. Feldman as one fraught with arguments and periods when they were
not talking. Therefore, she thought that this latest missive was part of this
pattern, and that the disagreement would be temporary. The subsequent events
proved that she was very wrong.

[
52
]

The text was sent around the time that Mr.
Feldman was going through a third divorce. He had asked Mr. Lande to lend him
money and Mr. Lande refused.

[
53
]

Mr. Feldman had also questioned Mr. Lande about his
spending in 2019. Mr. Feldman, joking he says, asked Mr. Lande if it might have
been gold that he saw in Uncle Ludwig’s bunker on the day that he was doing the
inventory.
Mr. Lande’s response of “None of your f—-ing
business” surprised him, as previously, the partners had never had any secrets with
each other.

[
54
]

Mr. Feldman then adopted a strategy to “smoke
Lande out”. The text message was part of that strategy.

[
55
]

The text message above was not the only missive
from Mr. Feldman to Mr. Lande. On May 20, 2020 he wrote:

I just want you to know that I have
not even begun to dig up your dark history and the endless lies, deceit and
fabrications of your business dealings, the origin of your investment funds
into your partnership and your windfalls from the Estate of your Uncle Ludwig.

[…]

I am going to give you one
opportunity to make things right for all the current living survivors of the
Holocaust and to fund education of children across America and Canada as to the
heinous crimes committed by the Nazi Regime and thereafter by Jews such as
yourself and your yellow toothed wife.

If you come clean, and when I say
clean, I mean perfectly clean with a full accounting of the gold, what you
spent, what is left over and where it will go, I will try my best to cushion
your fall. If you decide to be a greedy pig with your social ladder opportunist
wife, I promise that you will both be living on a hog farm eating truffles and
pig shit. The other alternative would be for both you and your wife to spend
many years in a prison cell, as you tried to do to me in a very underhanded
manner.

I am set to go all the way with
this file Irwin, and you know me. When I focus, I am 100% focused.
[8]

[
56
]

Mr. Feldman began to disseminate his allegations
about Mr. Lande and the source of his wealth. A special resolution that Mr.
Feldman orchestrated on March 11, 2020, in relation to the Sainte-Catherine
Street building, owned by Mr. Feldman and Mr. Lande with other partners,
provides the gist of the allegations:

WHEREAS the General Partners of
Montreal Media and Entertainment Building
Inc. and the
Limited Partners of Société en Commandite Montréal Média et Divertissement have
resolved to have Irwin Lande's shares and unit certificates and/or any trading
thereon suspended until such time as the Superior Court, District of Montreal,
Case No.: 500-17-110921-197 shall have determined whether or not your property
interests originate from public or private funds.
We have been made acutely
aware of Mr. Mr. Feldman's claim and supportive evidence which allege that your
funds, as well as those of your father, Martin Lande and mother, Mia Lande were
illegally misappropriated from Dr. Ludwig Littman Delphiner's Estate and that
the origin thereof may have been related to economic crimes against the Jewish
Holocaust and Victims Concentration Camps in Auschwitz
. The property
transfer rights shall be suspended until such time as this matter shall have
been resolved by way of a Court Judgment and not a settlement.
[9]

(The Court’s underlining)

[
57
]

This resolution led to a distinct lawsuit being
instituted by Mr. Lande on March 23, 2020
(the Commercial Proceedings)

to dissolve the partnership in the immovable. The other partners included Mr. Lande’s
nephews Jonathan Jacob and Andrew Feifer, through Sherry’s estate. Justice
Marie-Anne Paquette, as she then was, appointed MNP as the interim receiver.
[10]

[
58
]

Curiously, following Justice Paquette’s
judgment, Mr. Feldman drafted a “Long Form Affidavit”, dated March 31, 2020 and
deposited it directly at her office, but not into the Court file. It contains serious
affirmations about Nazi Gold stolen from Holocaust victims by Dr. Delphiner in
Poland, which gold would have been left to Martin, such that Mr. Lande and Sherry
ultimately became the benefactors
(the Long Form Affidavit)
.
[11]

Given that there will be a sealing order in respect of the Long Form Affidavit,
the Court will not provide a complete recital of the allegations, as they could
no doubt harm Mr. Lande’s and Ms. Pion’s reputations if additional elements of the
document were to find their way into the public domain. In the Court’s words,
here are some of the allegations most relevant to this judgment:

•

Mr. Feldman’s story begins at the time of the
probate of Dr. Delphiner’s will in 1983. He alleges that Mr. Lande and his
father forged the will and had him witness it, although he had never met Dr.
Delphiner.

•

He alleges having been with Mr. Lande and Martin
to conduct an estate inventory of the home of Dr. Delphiner. “
While
conducting an inventory of the assets I discovered a concrete encased room
measuring approximately 12'x 9' in the basement (lower level) in which I
observed 8 palettes of stacked metal bars
.” He
now assumes that they were gold.

•

He believes that Dr. Delphiner was a Waffen S.S.
officer, with Adolf Hitler's German Third Reich regime at the Auschwitz death
camps in Nazi occupied Poland during the Second World War, which gave him
access to this gold.

•

Mr. Feldman went as far as to visit Dr.
Delphiner’s former home with a real estate agent on the evening of January 7,
2020. He affirms having seen a one-pour concrete German-fashioned bunker which
measured exactly 9' by 12', equipped with a concealed steel-reinforced panic
door, battery remote lock button, surrounded by 3 to 4 feet thick cement walls
with no ventilation.

•

Assuming that the Nazi Gold had been stored
there, Mr. Feldman informed some of his partners in the Sainte-Catherine Street
building and in March convened an informal emergency meeting to pass the
special resolution, excluding Mr. Lande and the Feifers.

•

He alleges that a friend of Mr. Lande’s, Howard
Colton, offered him $30,000,000 for his interest in the partnership and to drop
his allegations (the Court will return to this);

[
59
]

One of many extracts that caught the Court’s
attention is the following:

On September 8, 2019, I started
taunting Irwin with text messages asking him to share 50% of his Uncle Ludwig's
lottery with his brother (GJF) or otherwise turn himself in to the Police. I
intended to smoke him out of his mansion on Place de Ramezay and get him to
admit his atrocities on the Holocaust victims. Instead, he threatened me with
Police charges which he never followed through with in September, October and
November 2019, until he discovered that I had contacted the MRQ Denunciation
Department in Rimouski (see attached text messages from Irwin).
[12]

[
60
]

This seems to have been part of Mr. Feldman’s
strategy to “smoke out” Mr. Lande.

[
61
]

The Long Form Affidavit was seemingly a work in
progress. There is another document in the record, the
“Final Revised Long
Form Summary”
dated April 19, 2021, which contains even more detail.
[13]
The following allegation sets
the tone:

« The gold bars stolen out of pure
greed, should have been rightfully returned to the Holocaust Survivors, Jews
and Non-Jews alike. The Landes personal greed and their plan to appropriate, by
false testament, the gold bullion bars for their own desires, took them down
the appalling path they embarked upon, and which Irwin Lande and his wife
Claude are still clearly on. They both have no sense of discretion or humility
in exposing their luxurious lifestyles to their new social circles, ever since
Mia Lande died in 2015. Living on pure blood money is exactly how I
characterize this story.

[
62
]

Jonathan Jacob Feifer gave his perspective to
the Court. He received a call from Mr. Feldman in November 2019. The latter was
anxious to know how much he and his brother Andrew had inherited from their
mother, Sherry. If he did not answer, Mr. Feldman would assume that they had
received $30 million.

[
63
]

Mr. Feifer tried to dissuade Mr. Feldman from
his belief that Dr. Delphiner had been an SS officer. He told him that Dr.
Delphiner had been a decorated Austrian soldier in World War II. Mr. Feifer was
given the medal by his grandmother, Mia.

1.7

Why did Mr. Feldman “Investigate”?

[
64
]

How did Mr. Feldman conclude that his partner
was living off the proceeds of Nazi Gold?

[
65
]

One of his initial mandates as a young lawyer
was the preparation of the will of Dr. Delphiner, a mandate given to him
by Martin. It was an English form will, which Mr. Feldman witnessed,
despite not being in the presence of the testator. His assistant was the other
witness. Mr. Feldman says that he regrets his involvement. This said, the Court
need not discuss the will further, as it is the subject of a judgment rendered
by Justice Philipps.
[14]

[
66
]

As the Court has said, after the death of Dr.
Delphiner, Mr. Feldman attended the house with Martin and Mr. Lande. He did an
inventory. It was during this visit that he claims to have seen the bunker with
the gold bars as well as a picture of Dr. Delphiner in an SS uniform. He asked
Mr. Lande whether Dr. Delphiner was a Nazi. According to Mr. Feldman, he
responded affirmatively, adding that he was a good Nazi.

[
67
]

Mr. Feldman’s real obsession with the Nazi Gold
theory seems to have begun with his suspicions over the money that his partner
was spending to renovate his residence in an expensive and opulent manner. Mr.
Feldman believed that the money that Mr. Lande was paying to contractors went
well beyond the income that he could generate from the partners’ business
ventures.

[
68
]

In fact, based on an originating application
filed by Mr. Lande and Ms. Pion in an action against their contractor, Mr.
Feldman believed that an amount in excess of $30 million had been paid to the
contractor.
[15]

Questioned on this amount, Mr. Lande could not understand the paragraph relied
on by Mr. Feldman. Ms. Pion believes that the couple spent around $18 million
but noted that her husband paid all the bills. The matter was ultimately
settled.

[
69
]

32

Quebec civil law does not provide
for a specific form of action for interference with reputation.  The basis
for an action in defamation in Quebec is found in art. 1457
C.C.Q.
,
which lays down the general rules that apply to questions of civil
liability.  Thus, in an action in defamation, the plaintiff must
establish, on a balance of probabilities, the existence of injury, of a
wrongful act, and of a causal connection, as in the case of any other action in
civil, delictual or quasi‑delictual liability.
(See N.
Vallières,
La presse et la diffamation
(1985), at
p. 43;
Houde v. Benoit
, [1943] Que. K.B. 713, at
p. 720;
Société Radio‑Canada v. Radio Sept‑Îles Inc.
,

1994 CanLII 5883 (QC CA)
,
[1994] R.J.Q. 1811 (C.A.)
, at p. 1818
.)

33

To demonstrate the first element of
civil liability, the existence of injury, the plaintiff must convince the judge
that the impugned remarks were defamatory. The concept of defamation has
been defined in several ways over the years.  Generally speaking, it is
held that defamation [TRANSLATION] “consists in the communication of spoken or
written remarks that cause someone to lose in estimation or consideration, or
that prompt unfavourable or unpleasant feelings toward him or her” (
Radio
Sept‑Îles
,
supra
, at p. 1818).

34

Whether remarks are defamatory is
determined by applying an objective standard (
Hervieux‑Payette v.
Société Saint‑Jean‑Baptiste de Montreal
,
1997 CanLII 8276 (QC CS)
,
[1998]
R.J.Q. 131 (Sup. Ct.)
, at p. 143,
reversed on other grounds by
Société
Saint-Jean-Baptiste de Montreal v. Hervieux-Payette
,
2002 CanLII 8266 (QC CA)
,
[2002] R.J.Q.
1669 (C.A.)
).  In other words, we must ask whether
an ordinary person would
believe that the remarks made, when viewed as a whole, brought discredit on the
reputation of another person.
On this point, we should note that words
may be defamatory because of the idea they expressly convey, or by the
insinuations that may be inferred from them.  In
Beaudoin v. La
Presse Ltée
,
1997 CanLII 8365 (QC CS)
,
[1998] R.J.Q. 204 (Sup. Ct.)
,
at p. 211,
Senécal J. provided a good summary of the approach to be
taken in determining whether particular remarks are defamatory in nature:

[TRANSLATION]  “The form in which the libel is expressed is of little
import; it is the result achieved in the mind of the reader that creates the
delict.”  The defamatory allegation or imputation may be direct, or it may
be indirect, “by simple allusion, insinuation or irony, or be made
conditionally, as an expression of doubt, or hypothetically.”  Often, the
allegation or imputation “is conveyed to the reader by way of a simple
insinuation, an interrogative sentence, a reference to a rumour, mention of
information that has infiltrated the public awareness, juxtaposition of
unrelated facts that, together, take on the appearance of being related”.

The words must
also be interpreted in their context. For instance, “it is not possible to
isolate a passage from a text and complain of it, if the entire text sheds a
different light on that excerpt”.  On the other hand, “it matters little
that the elements of which it is composed are true if the text as a whole
conveys a message that is contrary to reality”.  In fact, truth or reality
may be distorted by half‑truths, selective compilation, omissions, and so
on. “We must consider a newspaper article or radio broadcast as a whole, and
the sentences and words must be interpreted by reference to one another.”

35

However, a person who has made remarks
that are deemed to be defamatory will not necessarily be civilly liable for
them. The plaintiff must further demonstrate that the person who made the
remarks committed a wrongful act.  In
La responsabilité
civile
(5th ed. 1998), at pp. 301‑2, J.-L. Baudouin
and P. Deslauriers point out that in defamation cases, the wrongful act
may derive from two types of conduct, one malicious and the other merely
negligent:

[TRANSLATION]  The
first is an act in which the defendant, knowingly, in bad faith, with intent to
harm, attacks the reputation of the victim and tries to ridicule or humiliate
him or her, expose the victim to the hatred or contempt of the public or a
group. The second results from conduct in which there is no intent to
harm, but in which the defendant has nonetheless interfered with the reputation
of the victim through the defendant’s temerity, negligence, impertinence or
carelessness.  Both kinds of conduct constitute a civil fault and entitle
the victim to reparation, and there is no difference between them in terms of
the right.  In other words, we must refer to the ordinary rules of civil
liability and resolutely abandon the false idea that defamation is only the
result of an act of bad faith where there was intent to harm.

36

Based on the description of these two
types of conduct, we can identify three situations in which a person who made
defamatory remarks could be civilly liable.  The first occurs when a
person makes unpleasant remarks about a third party, knowing them to be
false.  Such remarks could only have been made maliciously, with the
intention to harm another person.  The second situation occurs when a
person spreads unpleasant things about someone else, when he or she should have
known them to be false.  A reasonable person will generally refrain from
giving out unfavourable information about other people if he or she has reason
to doubt the truth of the information.  The third case, which is often
forgotten, is the case of a scandalmonger who makes unfavourable but true
statements about another person without any valid reason for doing so.
(See
J. Pineau and M. Ouellette,
Théorie de la responsabilité
civile
(2nd ed. 1980), at pp. 63‑64.)

bring Mr. Lande into disrepute, Mr. Feldman chose to believe only what he
wanted to believe. To make such damaging allegations founded on a very
incomplete investigation is not the conduct of a reasonable person and is, in
and of itself, a fault:

[40] The reasonable person acts in
an ordinar­ily informed and diligent manner. He or she shows concern for others
and takes the necessary precautions to avoid causing them reasonably
foreseeable injury (
Ouellet v. Cloutier
,
1947 CanLII 35 (SCC)
, [1947]
S.C.R. 521, at p. 526). He or she respects fundamental rights and therefore
cannot disregard the protection estab­lished in the charters. Since the
standards maintained by the reasonable person are consistent with
Charter

values, he or she is careful not to violate the rights of others.
[75]

[
209
]

The information presented to the Court does not hold up to even
modest scrutiny. The record of Dr. Delphiner’s arrival in Halifax in 1926 and
his journey to Montreal is clear. However, there is no record of a departure
from Canada of this naturalized Canadian subsequent to his arrival, or of his
return after the Second World War. On the contrary, the records of his employer
demonstrate that Dr. Delphiner was in Canada in 1940!
[76]

[
210
]

What is more, as the text message of September 2019 demonstrates, Mr. Feldman’s
vendetta against his former partner began long before he had any significant
information on Dr. Delphiner. As he said in the Long Form Affidavit, his real
goal vis-à-vis Mr. Lande was to “smoke him out”.
[77]
The
“investigation” really only began in November 2019
[78]
and
there was still a lot of information to be obtained in the late winter and
spring of 2020.
[79]

[
211
]

The Final Revised Long Form Summary of April 2021 also bears this
out. Mr. Feldman’s student, Ms. Silverman, was working in the
investigation in April of 2020,
[80]
and
apparently found evidence of the death of a Romanian Ludwig Delphiner in
Ukraine in 1941. This discovery led Mr. Feldman to believe that:

“that Jewish Ludwig Delfiner's
identity was stolen upon his death and sold by Martin Lande to an assumed
“Uncle” and used in the Nazi SS Unit in Auschwitz to effectively serve and
thereafter flee in 1951 from the Ally forces after the fall of the Third Reich.
It is far too circumstantial that one Ludwig Delfiner, Merchant, is murdered in
the Holocaust in 1941 and the other a Chemist starts a new life in Canada in
1951, with vast amounts of gold bars appropriated during the Shoah.”
[81]

[
212
]

Two conclusions flow from this conclusion of Mr. Feldman. Firstly,
it seems to be an unreasonable and self-serving assumption that Martin sold the
identity of a deceased person, post 1941, to the individual who became a vice-president
of Abbott Laboratories, especially since that person had been in Canada since
1926, as shown by the very disembarkation records that Mr. Feldman had himself obtained.
Moreover, Martin did not arrive in Canada until the early fifties, making it extremely
improbable that Dr. Delphiner would have purchased his identity from Martin. In
addition, the collection of the facts, purportedly supporting the Nazi Gold
story, was far from complete when the vendetta against Mr. Lande began.

[
213
]

It was certainly incomplete when the resolution in relation to the Sainte-Catherine
Street property was adopted in March 2020.

[
214
]

Other elements of the Final Revised Long Form Summary support the
conclusion that the investigation was very incomplete when the allegations were
first made. The circumstances of the burial were still being investigated in
late May 2020.
[82]
Alan Delfiner was only spoken to in late May 2020.
[83]

[
215
]

Finally, several of the elements relied upon by Mr. Feldman to
support his allegations seem to be imagined. One of these is the uncorroborated
story related by Mr. Feldman that three safes were dropped into the Landes’
home by crane at 2:00 a.m. on December 11, 2019.
[84]

Equally fabricated is the allegation that the gold is stored in two exterior
storage tunnels and an interior depot.
[85]
The
testimony of Mr. Lagacé and the visit to the home clearly refute this idea.
Moreover, if the gold bars were hidden as Mr. Feldman suggests, how is Mr.
Lande using them to finance his lifestyle?

[
216
]

Even Mr. Feldman’s daughter confirms that “
We’re
going to get caught up in his imagination
” in
the short film.
[86]

[
217
]

In sum, even though Mr. Feldman had only a smattering of information
in the fall of 2019 and the winter of 2020, he still made egregious accusations
about Mr. Lande and Ms. Pion living off the avails of Nazi Gold. He was clearly
in a situation where he should have known that there was a good chance that his
accusations would prove to be false or were false. In disseminating them as he
did, Mr. Feldman did not act as a reasonable person and committed a fault.

[
218
]

There was also broad public dissemination of the allegations by Mr.
Feldman, the scope of which clearly demonstrates that his intent was to harm
Mr. Lande. If his sole purpose had been to seek restitution for Holocaust victims,
he might have limited his investigation to really trying to identify who Dr.
Delphiner was. Mr. Feldman did not do this. Instead, by his own admission, he communicated
the story to a large swath of individuals, including the Wiseman, Eisenberg, Bultz,
Brassgold and Colton families, Peter Politis, David R’Bibo, Mtre Caroline
Duval, Dr. Faez Faruqi, Vincent Griffo, Alice Markarian, Rabbi Moishe
Krazanski, Charles Jacobs (Mr. Lande’s accountant), Roy Potts, Sorab Alavi,
Jean-Pierre Lagacé, Jean-François Cloutier and his colleague Jonathan Fortin,
Menachem Kaiser and Billie Mintz.

[
219
]

The communication to journalists and Billie Mintz adds to the
gravity of the fault as it is demonstrative of the desire of Mr. Feldman to
harm Mr. Lande and Ms. Pion on a broader basis.

[
220
]

In addition, once Mr. Feldman had shared his story with the media,
he lost any control over how it would be diffused. From the Mintz film, one
sees that the story was shared by Mr. Mintz or his entourage with at least one
CBC reporter, and the Court has already alluded to the numerous people and
organizations that Mr. Cloutier, simply doing his job, communicated with.

[
221
]

As Justice Lalonde stated in
Tremblay c. Gordon
, this public communication
made in a malicious way constitutes a fault:

[60]        La faute peut résulter
de deux types de conduite :  une conduite malveillante ou une conduite
négligente.

[61]        En l’espèce, nous
sommes dans la situation selon laquelle le défendeur, sciemment, de mauvaise
foi, avec l’intention de nuire, s’attaque à la réputation de la victime et
cherche à la ridiculiser, à l’humilier, à l’exposer à la haine ou au mépris du
public ou d’un groupe visé, ici, la clientèle cible de Me Tremblay.

[62]        Indubitablement, le
Tribunal est d’avis que Gordon a commis une faute sanctionnable en propageant
par méchanceté certains propos qu’il savait faux à propos de Me Tremblay.
[87]

[
222
]

The scope of the dissemination is also relevant to the discussion of
the harm suffered by Mr. Lande and Ms. Pion.
[88]

[
223
]

The Court acknowledges that its findings here differ in some measure
with the ones that it reached in the
Feifer
matter. However, in the
present file the evidence is more complete.

[
224
]

Much more than the video, that the Court referred to in the
Feifer

judgment, was provided to the Journal de Montreal. The investigative work of
the journalists added to the scope of the dissemination.

[
225
]

The videos that discredit Mr. Lande were widely distributed; Ms.
Pion received them from third parties.

[
226
]

Then there are the Billie Mintz films. Any person with a bit of
ingenuity could easily determine that the partner that Mr. Feldman refers to is
Mr. Lande, and that the voice he uses, without having obtained consent, is Mr.
Lande’s. The films could easily cause a reasonable person to cast doubt on the
honesty of Mr. Lande and his father, Martin, even though it does not paint a
favourable picture of Mr. Feldman.

6.3

The Gravity of the Allegations

6.3.1

The Landes’ Personal Life

[
227
]

The Court considered this question in the
Feifer
judgment and
while concluding that they were damaging to Andrew and Jonathan Jacob Feifer,
given their personal situations, not being in Montreal and the lack of evidence
showing that their reputations were harmed in their own communities, the
damages awarded might be described as somewhat modest.

[
228
]

The situation is different here.

[
229
]

Firstly, there is uncontradicted evidence that the reputations of Mr.
Lande and Ms. Pion suffered a significant blow. It is true that Mr. Lande
did not give specific names of former friends who are now keeping their
distance, but Ms. Pion’s testimony was quite precise in this regard. What is
more is that for many years Ms. Pion worked hard to be accepted in the Jewish
community, including hosting Shabbat dinners and other events for her Jewish
friends. Her hospitality was frequently reciprocated. The scale and frequency
of these social interactions in the community have drastically diminished.

[
230
]

Who knows if the Landes will ever regain the same level of
acceptance that they once enjoyed in the Montreal Jewish community? In
addition, the stain on their reputations goes beyond Montreal. Howard Colton
noted that the story was being discussed in Florida. And what about the Billie
Mintz film? With it in the public domain, the story may not soon go away.

[
231
]

There is another distinguishing factor from the Feifer’s situation,
the article in the Journal de Montréal, which also appeared in Le Journal de
Québec, on TVA Nouvelles and in The Canadian.
[89]
In
the latter three publications the address of the Landes’ home is provided via a
screen shot of a Remax Web page. The information diffused to the public
included:

Le développeur d’une des maisons
les plus chères au Québec poursuit son partenaire d’affaires en diffamation,
après que celui-ci eut allégué qu’il aurait dissimulé dans sa résidence plus de
180 M$ en lingots d’or qui proviendraient des nazis.
[90]

[
232
]

For the Court, the gravity of this statement goes beyond the
Holocaust aspect. The house became a potential target… it was full of gold
bars!

[
233
]

The house was targeted by vandals, even before the articles in the
press. Although, Mr. Feldman denies involvement in the graffiti, in the recent
past he had hired thugs to disrupt the Bultz wedding. The modus operandi was
somewhat similar. However, even if the Court cannot conclude that he hired the
perpetrators of the graffiti, the fact that the incident happened at a time
when the life of the Landes was shrouded in Mr. Feldman’s allegations gave
them reasonable cause to think that there was a relation.

[
234
]

It certainly gave them reason to believe that the allegations were
having a negative effect on their personal security. Then there were the
newspaper articles, which could only serve to exacerbate their fear.

6.3.2

Mr. Lande’s Business Relationships,
Opportunities and Existing Buildings

[
235
]

Mr. Lande’s business relationships are another aspect of his life
that have been affected by the actions and allegations of Mr. Feldman. He is no
longer able to get financing for some of his ventures from Desjardins, with
whom he had developed an excellent relationship. This had a particular impact
on the Blainville shopping centre that the partners still own.

[
236
]

The fall out with Mr. Feldman also led to the divesture of several
buildings, in relation to which Mr. Lande claims damages.

[
237
]

Finally, there is his affirmation that his preoccupation with the
allegations, and the fatigue that they caused him, made it impossible for him
to pursue business opportunities.

[
238
]

On these aspects of his claim, the Court believes that Mr. Lande has
overstated the impact of Mr. Feldman’s actions.

[
239
]

While the Court can accept that, as he stated, Mr. Lande was
consumed by the dispute with Mr. Feldman, it cannot accept that this state of
mind prevented him from seeking out other business opportunities. With respect,
Mr. Lande remained focused on business opportunities, those that would remove
Mr. Feldman from any ownership position in their buildings, even those
that were held with other parties. This course of action is perhaps
understandable in the circumstances but belies Mr. Lande’s affirmation that he
was unfocused.  He was focused: on punishing his partner.

[
240
]

Moreover, he often adopted a pattern of behaviour that was designed
to enhance his personal position, the whole to the detriment of Mr. Feldman,
sometimes seeking to become the owner of different buildings that they owned
together or with others at modest cost to himself.

[
241
]

More particularly in relation to the Blainville shopping centre, the
Court retains from the judgments of Justice Sheehan that Mr. Lande’s own actions
(initially trying to purchase the property for himself) made it difficult to sell
the property and this has led to the current issues with Desjardins around the
financing of this property.

[
242
]

He also tried to buy the Sainte-Catherine Street building for
himself at a bargain price.

[
243
]

Mr. Lande asked for the partition of at least eight other properties
in a judicial application decided by Justice Beaugé.
[91]
Six
of these properties had other partners with significant ownership positions,
like the Sainte-Catherine Street building. To be fair, one of the partners in
these other properties was Issie Wiseman, who had signed the special
resolution, but there is little or no evidence in the record as to any efforts
made by Mr. Lande to discuss the allegations with these other partners, or
more importantly, to solicit their interest in buying out the shares of Mr.
Feldman.

[
244
]

One might also ask why, in July 2021, it was necessary to sell these
buildings. Mr. Lande argues that it was impossible for him to work with
Mr. Feldman. However, as the Court has said, Mr. Feldman only had a minority
position in six of the buildings that were the object of the Beaugé judgment.

[
245
]

As for the buildings that they held jointly, the evidence around the
difficulty in the management of them does not fully support Mr. Lande’s
affirmation that he needed to sell them. While the exact date that Mr. Feldman
had to move out of the LGIF/Landfeld offices is not fully clear, from the
Costom judgment, it appears that this move was in June 2020 at the latest. From
then on it appears that Mr. Lande was managing the properties himself. Mr. Potts
was only taking instructions from Mr. Lande. Why was it necessary to take a
judicial application to end the indivision one year later? What efforts were
made to find a partner to buy out Mr. Feldman’s share in these buildings? Proof
on the real difficulties in managing the buildings and the efforts to find
other partners is absent. The Court cannot draw the conclusion that the rush to
sell the buildings is fully attributable to Mr. Feldman’s allegations. It seems
that other solutions, less damaging to all, were not considered.

[
246
]

This said, the Court acknowledges that Mr. Lande was not required to
remain in indivision with Mr. Feldman, but if he had free rein in the management
of the jointly held properties, why rush to sell the properties?

[
247
]

As to the harm caused by the fading relationship with Desjardins,
the Court does not have sufficient evidence of the cost of any refinancing of
his properties to evaluate any damages caused to Mr. Lande by Mr. Feldman
having poisoned the relationship with Desjardins.

6.4

The Damages

6.4.1

Moral Damages

[
248
]

There is not an iota of doubt that Mr. Lande and Ms. Pion are
entitled to moral damages for the harm that Mr. Feldman’s actions and
affirmations have caused to their reputations and due to the stress that they
have suffered and continue to suffer.

[
249
]

The amounts that they claim are substantial:

A) Damages to their honour and
reputation vis-à-vis their friends, family, social acquaintances, neighbours,
etc.: $1.5 million;

B) Damages to their honour and
reputation vis-à-vis their business relations and associates, partners,
bankers, etc.: $3.5 million;

C) […]

D) Damages to their private life:
$500,000;

E) Damages to their rights to
personal security, safety, freedom and inviolability, including threats and
attempts at extorsion: $2.5 million;
[92]

[
250
]

Based on the evidence, the Court cannot make the same distinctions
as to where or in relation to what aspects of the Landes’ lives the damages
were suffered. The Court will make a global award in moral damages.

[
251
]

The real damages were suffered in relation to the private lives of
Mr. Lande and Ms. Pion, whether it be in relation to loss of friendships, loss
of esteem in the community, or fear for their security.

[
252
]

While there was some evidence that their “friendship” with their
account managers at Desjardins was harmed by Mr. Feldman’s actions, that was a
passing relationship driven on both sides by commercial interests.

[
253
]

The judgment of the Supreme Court of Canada in
Cinar
Corporation v. Robinson
provides guidance as to how the Court should
quantify non-pecuniary damages:

[105]

In Quebec, the quantum of non-pecuniary damages is
generally assessed by combining a conceptual approach, a personal approach, and
a functional approach:
St-Ferdinand
, at paras. 72-73, 75 and
77;
Gauthier v. Beaumont
,
1998 CanLII 788 (SCC)
,
[1998] 2 S.C.R. 3
, at
para.
101
. The conceptual approach measures loss “based on an appreciation
of the objective seriousness of the injury”:
Stations de la Vallée de
Saint-Sauveur inc. v. M.A.
,
2010 QCCA 1509
,
[2010] R.J.Q. 1872
,
at para.
83
,
per
Kasirer J.A. The personal approach
“seeks to evaluate, from a subjective point of view, the pain and inconvenience
resulting from the injuries suffered by the victim”:
St-Ferdinand
,
at para.
75,
citing A. Wéry, “L’évaluation judiciaire des dommages non pécuniaires résultant
de blessures corporel les: du pragmatisme de l’arbitraire?”,
[1986] R.R.A. 355
.
The functional approach
seeks to calculate the cost of measures that could provide solace to the
victim:
Andrews
, at p. 262. These
approaches “apply jointly, and thereby encourage a personalized evaluation” of
non-pecuniary damages:
St-Ferdinand
, at para. 80.

[106]

In addition to applying these approaches, courts assessing
non-pecuniary damages should compare the case at hand to other analogous cases
in which non-pecuniary damages were awarded:
Stations de la Vallée
,
at para. 83. They must attempt to treat “like cases alike” (
ibid.
), by
giving roughly similar compensation to victims whose injuries are alike when
assessed from the point of view of the combined approaches discussed above.
However, it is not helpful to compare cases where non-pecuniary damages are
capped to those where they are not. Arguments to the effect that a victim of
copyright infringement should not receive more compensation for non-pecuniary
damages than an accident victim rendered quadriplegic carry no weight, since
the
Andrews
cap applies as binding precedent in one case but
not in the other.

[107]

In this case, the trial judge relied heavily on the
personal approach, emphasizing the subjective impact of the infringement of
copyright on
Robinson
’s mental state and
personal life.  He bolstered his analysis by comparing
Robinson
’s anguish to the similar level of anguish
experienced by the plaintiff in the defamation
case
Société
Radio-Canada v. Gilles E. Néron Communication Marketing inc.
,
2002 CanLII 41249 (QC CA)
,
[2002] R.J.Q.
2639 (C.A.)
, aff’d
2004 SCC 53
,
[2004] 3 S.C.R. 95
. In
Néron
,
the Court of Appeal confirmed an award of non-pecuniary damages in the amount
of $300,000.  The trial judge also looked to the
Hill

case,
in
which this Court awarded $300,000 in general damages to a victim of defamation.
He correctly took into account the fact that
Hill
had been
decided over a decade before the case at hand, and that a valid comparison
required the amount awarded to be adjusted for inflation.

[108]

I agree with the trial judge that
Robinson
’s
non-pecuniary damages are analogous to those claimed by a victim of defamation.
The product of
Robinson
’s artistic exertions
was taken from him and the integrity of his personal creative process was
violated, causing deep psychological suffering. These harms are similar to
those suffered by a victim of defamation.
[93]

[149]

Given the restoration
of the trial judge’s award for non-pecuniary damages, it is not unimportant to
consider some of his words:

[981]

La preuve par son entourage de son atteinte psychologique
est non contredite, claire, précise et concordante
.

[982]
Il y a un lien direct entre le dommage et la faute des défendeurs.

[983]

Le demandeur a dû attendre plus de treize ans avant de
connaître l’aboutissement de cette odyssée judiciaire
. Comme son médecin
traitant l’a déclaré et il est non contredit, cette odyssée a un aspect
thérapeutique malgré tout.

[…]

[987]
Dans
Néron
[94]
,
la Cour d’appel du Québec a octroyé une somme de 300 000 $ à ce chapitre dans
une affaire où la Cour constate cinq années d’adversité et de souffrance
pendant le processus judiciaire.

[988]
La juge Mailhot, dans ce jugement majoritaire, écrit :

[102] De
même, en l'espèce, en situant les dommages moraux accordés en 2000 par le
premier juge dans l'ensemble des autres dommages octroyés, je ne trouve pas de
motif d'intervenir.  Un simple survol des pièces P-92 et P-89 permet de
comprendre l'état d'esprit de M. Néron tout au long des mois qui ont suivi les
événements, ses souffrances profondes, ses espoirs en l'avenir déçus par la
réalité qui ne lui a réservé qu'une perte de plus en plus aiguë dans sa
situation financière et dans sa situation personnelle.  Les douleurs
et
le désarroi
de M. Néron sont réels et le juge de première instance,
dont c'est la fonction première d'apprécier cette preuve, l'a, à mon avis,
correctement fait.

[103] Je
confirmerais donc les dommages moraux de 300 000 $.

[989]
La Cour suprême n’est pas intervenue sur cet aspect.

[990]
Le Tribunal fait siens les propos de la juge Mailhot et n’aurait
pas pu mieux dire.
[95]

(The
Court’s underlining) (References omitted)

[
254
]

It is perhaps difficult to find a case that is analogous to this
one, but the case of
Soliman v. Bordman
,
[96]
offers a degree of similarity. The impugned conduct is described as
follows:

[1]
In this action, the Plaintiff, Walied
Soliman, alleges that he has been defamed by the Islamophobic hate speeches of
the Defendant, Daniel Bordman. The alleged defamatory statements were video
streamed across the Internet from a newsroom studio at TAG TV and from the
Bordmans’ family home on various Internet social media and alternative news
media. Mr. Soliman asserts that Mr. Bordman, in addition to being a defamer, is
a hatemonger, a racist, and a member of the alt-right community of demagogues,
hatemongers, conspiracy theorists, and Islamophobes.

[
255
]

This is an example of the type of communication that was continually
published:

Now, the other thing he said is, it
was quite interesting, is that he [Mr. Soliman] would support Al Quds Day. Al
Quds Day is the march within Toronto that's supported by Islamic Iran. The
destroy Israel march. There was a Hezbollah flag flying this year. Lots of, I
did a whole live stream on it. Right? Bad News Bears. It's a pro-terrorist
march. It's supposed to be illegal, but it happened this year. So, he said he
would support that, but the only reason he would not support that is because he
has Jewish colleagues in his law firm, and if you want to get your points, he
told my business partner this, he's like "if you want to get your points
across in Canada, if you want to undermine Israel you got to play the long game
- you got to be smart about how you do it in Canadian politics. […]”
[97]

[
256
]

Justice Perrell awarded the sum of $500,000, noting that the posts
could be seen by millions of viewers.

[
257
]

The evidence here does not show that the allegations have been seen
by millions of viewers, but with the release of the Billie Mintz film the
number of people who might hear about the allegations will no doubt increase
and the consequent damage is ongoing.

[
258
]

On the other hand, the evidence here does not show the same degree
of “douleurs and désarroi” that Mr. Neron appears to have suffered
.
This
said, there is no doubt that the prejudice and harm caused to both Mr. Lande
and Ms. Pion is significant, for Ms. Pion, given the significant efforts that
she made to be accepted in the Jewish community and for Mr. Lande, given
the standing he and his family have long enjoyed in the community.

[
259
]

There are certain indignities that Mr. Lande suffered that Ms. Pion
was spared from. His personal financial information was communicated to
journalists and even the CRA and the IRS.

[
260
]

Accusations about his probity were made to Mr. Cormier.

[
261
]

Seemingly more in relation to Mr. Lande, Mr. Feldman also
communicated with his car dealer, his real estate agents, and even the mayor of
Bal Harbour.

[
262
]

Finally, there is the Gold Bars film. In it, Mr. Lande’s voice is
used without his consent. It is easy to identify who the film is referring to.
The short film is worse. It has a picture of Mr. Lande, complete with a
Hitler-like moustache. These actions were a clear invasion of privacy as set
out in
Aubry v. Éditions Vice-Versa inc.
:

52
In
Godbout v. Longueuil (City)
, the
Supreme Court held that the purpose of the protection accorded to privacy is to
guarantee a sphere of individual autonomy for all decisions relating to
“choices that are of a fundamentally private or inherently personal nature”
(para. 98).  If the purpose of the right to privacy guaranteed by
s. 5
of the
Quebec
Charter
is to protect a
sphere of individual autonomy, that right must include the ability to control
the use made of one’s image, since the right to one’s image is based on the
idea of individual autonomy, that is, on the control each person has over his
or her identity.  It can also be stated that this control implies a
personal choice.  It should be noted, finally, that art. 36 of the
new
Civil Code of Québec
, S.Q. 1991, c. 64
, although not applicable here, confirms this
interpretation since it recognizes that the use of a person’s name, image, likeness
or voice for a purpose other than the legitimate information of the public is
an invasion of privacy.
[98]

[
263
]

The actions of Mr. Feldman are akin to the tort of public disclosure
of private facts, discussed by Justice Kristjanson in
Yenovkian v. Gulian
:

[170] With these three torts all
recognized in Ontario law, the remaining item in the “four-tort catalogue” of
causes of action for invasion of privacy is the third, that is, publicity
placing the plaintiff in a false light. I hold that this is the case in which
this cause of action should be recognized. It is described in § 652E of the
Restatement

as follows:

Publicity Placing Person in
False Light

One who gives publicity to a matter
concerning another that places the other before the public in a false light is
subject to liability to the other for invasion of his privacy, if

(a) the false light in which the
other was placed would be highly offensive to a reasonable person, and

(b) the actor had knowledge of or
acted in reckless disregard as to the falsity of the publicized matter and the
false light in which the other would be placed.
[99]

[

What is the appropriate amount of punitive damages? Determining the

[136]

As discussed, punitive damages are assessed by looking to the purposes they
serve — prevention, deterrence, and denunciation.  Factors to be
considered include the gravity of the debtor’s fault; the debtor’s patrimonial
situation; the extent of the reparation for which the debtor is already liable
to the creditor; and the fact that the payment of damages will be wholly or
partly assumed by a third person:  art. 1621
CCQ
.  I also
note that, in Quebec civil law, “it is perfectly acceptable to use punitive
damages, as is done at common law, to relieve a wrongdoer of its profits where
compensatory damages would amount to nothing more than an expense paid to earn
greater profits while flouting the law”:
Richard
, at para. 206.

[137]

In addition, particular attention must be paid to the gravity of the debtor’s
fault, which “is undoubtedly the most important factor”:
Richard
,

wrongful conduct of the wrongdoer and the seriousness of the infringement of
the victim’s rights”
(ibid.).

CCQ

para. 249. However, in cases where the gravity of the conduct warrants it,
punitive damages reaching $1,000,000 or more have been awarded:
Markarian;
Whiten v. Pilot Insurance Co
.,
2002 SCC 18
,

[2002] 1 S.C.R. 595
.

rejette l’utilisation de la théorie de la perte de chance pour pallier
l’absence de preuve sur le lien de causalité. Pour que la théorie s’applique,
il faut donc que la preuve établisse que « la chance perdue soit
réelle
et sérieuse

et
que sa
réalisation soit
probable
».

[81]

En d’autres mots, une perte de chance peut devenir un préjudice

L’

locale 130

distinction

chance et le dommage pour lequel on réclame

il y a donc lieu de refuser de compenser la « perte de chance

because of its highly sensitive character, its dissemination would occasion an
affront to their dignity that society as a whole has a stake in protecting.

[…]

[35]

I hasten to say that applicants for an order making
exception to the open court principle cannot content themselves with an
unsubstantiated claim that this public interest in dignity is compromised any
more than they could by an unsubstantiated claim that their physical integrity
is endangered. Under
Sierra Club
, the applicant must show on the
facts of the case that, as an important interest, this dignity dimension of
their privacy is at “serious risk”. For the purposes of the test for
discretionary limits on court openness, this requires the applicant to show
that the information in the court file is sufficiently sensitive such that it
can be said to strike at the biographical core of the individual and, in the
broader circumstances, that there is a serious risk that, without an
exceptional order, the affected individual will suffer an affront to their
dignity.

[221]

In
the Court’s view, Plaintiffs have met this burden and the requested
sealing
order, greatly diminished from their initial request, is
appropriate save as regards exhibit P-11. Exhibits P-10, P-27 and P-37 are all
variations of Feldman’s Long Form Affidavit. All comprise a somewhat rambling
recounting of the allegations. Although, much of the content of the documents
relates to Lande and not to the Feifers, the Court considers that taken as a
whole, the content might be damaging to Plaintiffs.

[222]

Even
if the gist of Feldman’s allegations is already in the public domain, the
detail that he exposes in the documents that would be the object of a
sealing
order is not, so the order is appropriate.
[122]

(References omitted)

[
322
]

These words of the Supreme Court of Canada in
Sherman Estate v.
Donovan
are also relevant to the circumstances of the present matter:

[72]                          Where
dignity is impaired, the impact on the individual is not theoretical but could
engender real human consequences, including psychological distress (see
generally
Bragg
, at para. 23). La Forest J., concurring, observed in
Dyment

that privacy is essential to the well
‑
being of individuals (p.
427). Viewed in this way, a privacy interest, where it shields the core
information associated with dignity necessary to individual well-being, begins
to look much like the physical safety interest also raised in this case, the
important and public nature of which is neither debated, nor, in my view,
seriously debatable. The administration of justice suffers when the operation
of courts threatens physical well
‑
being because a
responsible court system is attuned to the physical harm it inflicts on
individuals and works to avoid such effects.
Similarly, in my view, a
responsible court must be attuned and responsive to the harm it causes to other
core elements of individual well
‑
being, including
individual dignity.
This parallel helps to
understand dignity as a more limited dimension of privacy relevant as an
important public interest in the open court context.

[73]                        I am
accordingly of the view that protecting individuals from the threat to their
dignity that arises when information revealing core aspects of their private
lives is disseminated through open court proceedings is an important public
interest for the purposes of the test.

[74]                        Focusing
on the underlying value of privacy in protecting individual dignity from the
exposure of private information in open court overcomes the criticisms that
privacy will always be at risk in open court proceedings and is theoretically
complex. Openness brings intrusions on personal privacy in virtually all cases,

but dignity as a public interest in protecting an individual’s core
sensibility is more rarely in play
. Specifically, and consistent with the
cautious approach to the recognition of important public interests, this
privacy interest, while determined in reference to the broader factual setting,

will be at serious risk only where the sensitivity of the information
strikes at the subject’s more intimate self
.
[123]

(The Court’s underlining)

[

It is perhaps a bit rich that Mr. Feldman asks for this information
to be under seal given that he made it his business to disseminate the same
sort of information about Mr. Lande. This, of course, is not principal
factor that the Court must consider. In a very similar matter, already referred
to,
Savoie c. Thériault-Martel
, Justice Morrison sets the factors for
the Court to consider:

[32]        En ce qui concerne la
prétention de Savoie à l’effet que son information financière constitue un
intérêt commercial important et qu’elle devrait être protégée par les
ordonnances de confidentialité recherchées, il est important de se rappeler que
selon l’art. 1621 C.C.Q.[13], lorsque la loi prévoit l’attribution de dommages
punitifs, comme dans le cas de l’art. 54.4 C.P.C., le Tribunal doit tenir
compte de la situation patrimoniale du débiteur.  Cela dit, l’information
financière dont demande Thériault-Martel par rapport à sa réclamation en
dommages punitifs s’agit-elle d’une importance personnelle et privée ou
s’agit-il, sur une base objective, dans l’intérêt du public de voir à la
confidentialité d’une telle information?

[33]        Certes, Savoie a un
intérêt privé à garder l’information confidentielle.  Il explique que le Groupe
Savoie emploie environ 1600 personnes avec qui le Groupe est appelé à négocier
les conditions de travail.  De plus, comme entrepreneur, il doit négocier le
développement de nouveaux projets.

[34]        Savoie craint que sa
capacité de négocier avec ses employés et avec des tiers soit diminuée s’il est
obligé de dévoiler son patrimoine personnel.

[35]        Cela est davantage
compliqué vu que les compagnies du Groupe Savoie sont, selon le procureur de
Savoie, intrinsèquement liées à sa personne et ce, à un tel point que pour
connaître la valeur de son patrimoine personnel on doit connaître la valeur de
toutes ses compagnies.

[36]        Il n’est donc pas difficile
de comprendre que la divulgation de sa situation patrimoniale représente pour
Savoie un inconvénient important.

[37]        Mais l’inconvénient
important n’est pas le test à appliquer.  La question est de savoir s’il existe
un intérêt public qui justifie que l’on garde confidentielle l’information en
question.
[129]

[
332
]

view the same result should apply here. It is true that Justice Morrison
rendered his judgment before some of the more recent decisions of the Supreme
Court of Canada. However, the information in exhibits P-87 to P-101 does not go
to Mr. Feldman’s more intimate self. Likely, every time he does a new
transaction, he needs to share some of this information.

another person, giving rise to punitive damages is an important element that a
court must consider in its award.

6.7

Injunctive Relief

[
334
]

Mr. Lande and Ms. Pion also ask for a permanent injunction to be
issued against Mr. Feldman. The essence of their demand is that Mr. Feldman
cease his violations of their fundamental rights.

[

In the initial Originating Application, the requested order was
quite general in scope, perhaps difficult to enforce. The Re-reamended
application provides for more focused orders.

[

There is precedent for this relief in defamation cases, although it
is exceptional. The comments of Justice Silcoff in the matter of
National
Bank of Canada c. Weir
provide insight into when the Court might use its
discretion to grant injunctive relief:

[42]            The Courts have
generally been reluctant to grant injunctive relief, on an interlocutory basis,
to restrain abusive and defamatory comments, in advance and in anticipation of
their having been made. There are abundant authorities, both from Québec and
from the common law jurisdictions in this regard. In
Champagne
v. Collège d’enseignement général et professionnel de Jonquière
, Rothman
JA. notes at page 16 :

The common law authorities in Canada and the U.K. have suggested the
guiding principle that
interlocutory injunctions should only be granted
to restrain in advance written or spoken words in the rarest and clearest of
cases
- where the words are so manifestly defamatory and impossible to
justify that an action in defamation would almost certainly succeed. Given the
value we place on freedom of expression, particularly in matters of public
interest, that guiding principle has much to recommend it.

In the present case,
I do not believe we can say, at this stage, that the past comments of Champagne
are manifestly defamatory and impossible to justify.

Nor do I believe we
can say what his future comments will be. Applications for orders involving
prior restraint of future comments or publications, the contents of which are
unknown, must obviously be viewed with the greatest of caution. (Woodward v.
Hutchins [1977] 2 All E.R. (Eng. C.A.), see Lord Denning pages 754, 755; Fraser
v. Evans
[1969] 1 All E.R. 8
, 12; Liverpool Household Stores Association v.
Smith [1887] Vol. XXXVII Ch. D. 170, 181)
There are, doubtless,
exceptional cases where it is perfectly clear that the past comments or
publications are such that all future comments or publications are bound to be
defamatory and unjustified as well, and must be restrained. This is not such a
case.

(our emphasis)

[43]            The facts and circumstances
in present matter constitute one such exceptional case referred to by Rothman
JA.

[…]

[45]            Moreover, seeing
the abundance and compelling nature of the damming evidence in the present
proceedings and, in particular, of the crusade like mission pursued by Weir to
defame the honour and reputation of the Bank and its representatives, to borrow
the language of Rothman JA.,
it is perfectly clear that the past comments or
publications are such that all future comments or publications are bound to be
defamatory and unjustified as well, and must be restrained
.
[130]

[
337
]

The same year, the Court of Appeal said this in
Prud'homme c.
Rawdon (Municipalité de)
:

[60]        Dans un premier temps,
le juge Rothman rappelle que la Cour supérieure a entièrement compétence pour
prononcer une ordonnance d'injonction interlocutoire afin d'interdire tous
propos diffamatoires, et ce, dans l'attente de l'audition au fond de l'action.

[61]        En deuxième lieu,
souligne-t-il, cette compétence sera exercée avec prudence.  Elle sera réservée
aux situations les plus claires et rares où le caractère diffamant ou injurieux
des propos est évident et ne peut être justifié d'aucune façon.  Encore là,
l'ordonnance d'injonction ne sera prononcée que si la preuve établit, de façon
prépondérante, que l'auteur a l'intention de récidiver.

[62]        Troisièmement, dans
tous les cas l'ordonnance recherchée doit viser des propos précis, et ce, pour
deux motifs.  D'abord, l'ordonnance en termes généraux qui interdit de diffamer
a pour effet de porter indûment atteinte à la liberté d'expression et a
nécessairement un effet de bâillon (chilling effect) pour la personne visée.
[131]

[
338
]

The Court considers that this situation is exceptional enough that
